I have resolved the issue in [json.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lz57zmm8/django/db/models/fields/json.py):

- Added [`HasKeyLookup.compile_json_path_final_key`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lz57zmm8/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L175-L177) and updated [`HasKeyLookup.as_sql`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lz57zmm8/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L200-L203) so that the final key in `has_key`, `has_keys`, and `has_any_keys` lookups is compiled as a JSON object key (`."<key>"`) rather than an array index (`[<int>]`) when the key is numeric.
- Added [`HasKeyOrArrayIndex`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lz57zmm8/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L257-L259) and used it in [`KeyTransformIsNull`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lz57zmm8/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L393-L414) and [`KeyTransformExact`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lz57zmm8/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L471-L483) so key transforms continue to support array index paths on SQLite and Oracle.
